references.text: Caiaphas's argument that it is better for one man to die for the people assumes the same fear that the nation will perish, as expressed in John 11:48.
This verse confirms that the council decided to kill Jesus to save the nation from the Romans, directly as a consequence of the fear in John 11:48.
The prophecy that Jesus should die for the nation and gather God's scattered children corresponds directly to the fear in John 11:48 that the nation will perish.
Here the Pharisees confess that they have accomplished nothing, since the whole world is going after Jesus, which confirms the fear in John 11:48 that everyone would believe in him.
The Jews express here that they are not allowed to put anyone to death, showing how they had to use Roman authorities to avoid the 'nation' perishing, as they feared in John 11:48.
